Definition: Beth-ha-Ram, a place East of the Jordan
BiblicalUsage: Beth-Aram means place of the height, and it is named once, in Joshua 13:27, among the towns in the valley given to Gad — Beth-aram and Beth-nimrah and Succoth, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon. A town east of the Jordan, listed with its neighbours and left there.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the towns across the Jordan were still God's gift, even when they sat outside the land most people picture.
